in five pages, team leaders approving for their teams, schedules as drafts until published, Ultra HA across two sites, site-loss drills, and do-not-call registers loaded once for many organisations.

Workforce in five pages: Workforce is now Today, Schedule, Requests, Plan and Settings, with one filter bar by site, team and queue. Your organisation's own sites are kept with its teams, and the service-level target comes from each queue's Service levels.

Time off: breaks, leave, training and every other reason an agent is away are one list of away types under Workforce Settings, called Time off everywhere. Each type says whether it is paid, counts against staffing, can be scheduled, needs approval and can be chosen on the desk. Changing how a type is paid, counted, scheduled or approved needs the Workforce permission; managing agents alone allows only its name, colour and whether it shows on the desk.

Team leaders and schedules: team leaders approve time off and swaps for their own teams, schedule changes stay drafts until a planner publishes them, and agents see My schedule on the desk. A published scheduling run updates each agent's desk once.

Ultra HA across two sites: an organisation can run on two sites at once, with the database confirming each write at both, messaging, recordings and caches kept per site, and calls routed through each site's own call servers and carriers. Each organisation has a home site, and a health check per site moves traffic away from a site that is down or being updated. Releases are installed one site at a time, with each site drained, updated, checked and put back, and a release whose database changes would break the running version is refused.

Site-loss drills: on Platform, Availability, a drill cuts one site or server off on purpose, counts every write made during the cut, and reports how long the takeover took and whether anything was lost. The runbook and help guide explain each step.

Resilient pair: the shared addresses now follow the database's primary, so a network cut between the two servers no longer leaves both holding them.

Do-not-call registers: a register can be uploaded as a zipped file, and a reseller can load a register once for all their organisations. A register can be fetched at once instead of waiting for its next refresh.

Live quality on chats and emails: a must-say line with a time limit is checked every half minute on written conversations, so it is raised on time even when nobody writes.

Caller verification and payment links: when a caller is verified, by a flow step, by voice, by a colleague or on their own PIN page, or a payment link is paid, the desk shows it at once instead of on its next check.

Fixes: calls through a carrier's second-site gateway count towards that carrier's status.

For platform operators: this release can only be installed on a server already running 0.1.81 or later."}
